findings.description: The call passes argc=6 but supplies 7 varargs (hsetex, key, keepttl, fields, integers[1], field, newobj). rewriteClientCommandVector (networking.c:4158) reads exactly argc varargs, so newobj (the new field value) is never consumed and the propagated command becomes 'HSETEX <key> KEEPTTL FIELDS 1 <field>' — 6 tokens, missing the value. On replicas and during AOF replay, hsetexParseArgs (t_hash.c:2214) hits 'i >= c->argc - 3' and returns an arity error, so the write is silently not applied: replicas diverge and the acknowledged increment is lost on AOF reload. The upstream fix (redis/redis#14224) uses argc=7, and this PR's own assert_replication_stream expects the 7-element '{hsetex h1 KEEPTTL FIELDS 1 f1 *}' and will fail.
findings.failureMode: Every HINCRBYFLOAT propagates a malformed HSETEX that errors on replicas and in AOF replay, so the incremented value is silently dropped — permanent master/replica divergence and data loss after AOF reload, plus the added replication test fails.
findings.title: rewriteClientCommandVector argc=6 drops the value argument, propagating a malformed HSETEX

findings.description: The base passed 'HASH_SET_TAKE_VALUE | HASH_SET_KEEP_TTL' to hashTypeSet; this diff leaves only HASH_SET_TAKE_VALUE. Without KEEP_TTL, hashTypeSet clears the field's expiry: listpackExUpdateExpiry(o, field, fptr, vptr, HASH_LP_NO_TTL) for LISTPACK_EX hashes (t_hash.c:961-963) and hfieldPersist(o, oldField) for HT hashes (t_hash.c:989-991). So on the master, HINCRBYFLOAT on a field with a TTL now silently removes the TTL — HTTL returns -1 — while the sibling hincrbyCommand still keeps the flag (t_hash.c:2506) and the upstream fix does not touch this line. It also reintroduces divergence in the opposite direction: the replica keeps its TTL via KEEPTTL and expires the field while the master retains it forever.
findings.failureMode: On the master, HINCRBYFLOAT on a field that has an expiration silently deletes the TTL (the field never expires), and replicas still expire it — wrong HTTL results and master/replica divergence.
findings.title: Dropping HASH_SET_KEEP_TTL removes the field TTL on the master itself

findings.description: The rewrite passes 7 robj* arguments (hsetex, c->argv[1], keepttl, fields, integers[1], c->argv[2], newobj) but declares argc=6; rewriteClientCommandVector (src/networking.c:4158) reads exactly argc varargs, so newobj (the value) is never consumed and the propagated command becomes 'HSETEX key KEEPTTL FIELDS 1 field'. In hsetexParseArgs (src/t_hash.c:2214) the FIELDS token at argv[3] satisfies i >= c->argc - 3 (3 >= 3) and is rejected with an arity error, so replicas log an error and skip the update and AOF records the malformed command; upstream PR redis/redis#14224 uses argc=7, and the added test's expected stream entry '{hsetex h1 KEEPTTL FIELDS 1 f1 *}' (7 tokens) cannot match the 6-token command produced.
findings.failureMode: Every propagated HINCRBYFLOAT errors out on replicas and in AOF replay, so the increment is silently lost, causing persistent master/replica divergence and lost updates on AOF reload.
findings.title: rewriteClientCommandVector argc=6 drops the value argument from propagated HSETEX

findings.description: The local hashTypeSet call had HASH_SET_KEEP_TTL removed. Inside hashTypeSet, KEEP_TTL is what preserves an existing field's TTL: for OBJ_ENCODING_LISTPACK_EX a set field's expiry is overwritten with HASH_LP_NO_TTL (src/t_hash.c:961-964) and for OBJ_ENCODING_HT hfieldPersist removes it (src/t_hash.c:989-991). The master now clears the field's TTL on every HINCRBYFLOAT (HTTL returns -1) while the propagated HSETEX KEEPTTL preserves it on the replica — the same divergence this PR fixes, inverted; upstream PR #14224 did not change this line.
findings.failureMode: On the master the field's TTL is silently discarded (the field never expires and HTTL reports -1) while replicas retain a TTL the master no longer has, producing master/replica divergence.
findings.title: HINCRBYFLOAT loses HASH_SET_KEEP_TTL, deleting the field TTL on the master

findings.description: The guard `if rendered is not None and not isinstance(rendered, str)` lets a None result fall through to `return rendered`, violating the declared `-> str`. Verified by running the repo's pinned basedpyright (~=1.31.0, strict mode via pyrightconfig.json): `template_renderer.py:40:16 - error: Type "str | None" is not assignable to return type "str" (reportReturnType)`, so the required Basedpyright Checks step in .github/workflows/style.yml fails. At runtime, if `execute_workflow_code_template` returns a mapping whose "result" is missing/None, `render_template` returns None and `TemplateTransformNode._run` raises TypeError on `len(rendered)` — a TypeError is not a TemplateRenderError, so it escapes the intended clean FAILED result and is caught only by Node.run's generic handler. Fix: `if not isinstance(rendered, str): raise TemplateRenderError("Template render result must be a string.")` then `return rendered`.
findings.failureMode: The repo's basedpyright CI gate fails deterministically on this line, and on the edge path where the executor result lacks a string "result" the node crashes with an uncaught TypeError instead of returning a FAILED NodeRunResult.
findings.title: render_template returns None despite -> str; basedpyright reportReturnType error

AutomationWizardSchema types expect as z.array(z.string()).optional() with no min-length, so [""] passes validation.
findings.failureMode: A custom trigger submitted after clearing the textarea (or with blank lines) contains empty-string event names in `expect`, which never match real events and corrupt the automation's expected-event list.
findings.title: Empty lines stored as empty-string expected events

findings.failureMode: Clearing the threshold input stores NaN in trigger.threshold for the work-pool template only, producing an inconsistent value and React 'Received NaN for value attribute' warnings.
findings.title: parseInt used without radix for threshold

findings.description: The new loop uses `j <= keys_result->numkeys`, iterating numkeys+1 times. On the extra iteration it reads keys_result->keys[numkeys], which is out of bounds: for numkeys<=6 the entry aliases the inline keysbuf (fresh results have pos=0, so argv[0] -- the command name -- is hashed as a phantom key; a stale nonzero pos can index argv out of bounds), for numkeys==6 it aliases the `keys` pointer field, and for numkeys>6 it reads past the heap array. It also writes slot_buffer[numkeys], a 4-byte heap overflow past the `numkeys * sizeof(int)` allocation, and dereferences argv[garbage] via this_key->ptr. Reached for every command with >=1 extracted key when cluster is enabled, via preprocessCommand -> extractKeysAndSlot (server.c:4136) and getSlotFromCommand (db.c:438).
findings.failureMode: In cluster mode, keyed commands corrupt the heap (OOB write), may crash on wild argv/keyReference reads, and almost always return CLUSTER_CROSSSLOT because the phantom argv[0] key hashes to a different slot -- so correct commands are wrongly rejected with a cross-slot error.
findings.title: Off-by-one loop in extractSlotFromKeysResult reads/writes out of bounds and returns spurious CROSSSLOT

findings.description: Lines 1110, 1120 and 1124 call malloc()/free() directly, violating the repository mandate (AGENTS.md rule 2) that all dynamic allocation in src/ use zmalloc/zfree so memory is tracked. The malloc result is also never NULL-checked: on allocation failure slot_buffer is NULL and `slot_buffer[j] = this_slot` dereferences it, whereas zmalloc would abort cleanly.
findings.failureMode: Memory for slot tracking is untracked by Redis's allocator accounting, and an OOM failure turns into a NULL-pointer write crash instead of the controlled zmalloc abort.
findings.title: extractSlotFromKeysResult uses raw malloc/free instead of mandatory zmalloc wrappers

findings.description: The new invite endpoint is decorated with @Roles("TEAM_MEMBER") while the PR contract, the new e2e spec (non-admin member must get 403), and the sibling organizations-teams-invite.controller.ts:33 all require TEAM_ADMIN. findings.description: handleShowReaderModeAction now returns displayView: .readerModeLongPressAction (was .readerMode in base, per git show of the same function). In BrowserViewController.handleDisplayActions, .readerMode calls toggleReaderMode() while .readerModeLongPressAction calls toggleReaderModeLongPressAction(), which calls profile.readingList.createRecordWithURL — an add-to-reading-list operation, not reader mode. ToolbarMiddleware dispatches GeneralBrowserActionType.showReaderMode on a plain tap of the reader mode toolbar button, so that tap now writes a Reading List record and never toggles reader mode.
findings.failureMode: Tapping the reader mode toolbar button adds the current page to the Reading List (with a 'Added to Reading List' toast) instead of entering/exiting reader mode.
findings.title: Reader mode tap adds page to Reading List instead of toggling reader mode

findings.description: The condition changed from 'currentURL.isWebPage() && !currentURL.isReaderModeURL' to 'currentURL.isWebPage() || currentURL.isReaderModeURL'. Reader-mode URLs (http://localhost:<port>/reader-mode/page?url=...) satisfy isWebPage(), so the only behavioral change is that reader-mode URLs are now kept instead of nil'd. handleCancelEditAction stores the URL in AddressBarState.url, and LocationView sets urlTextField.text = config.url?.absoluteString, displaying the raw internal URL. cancelEditMode is invoked on .tabs, .menu and .cancelEdit toolbar taps.
findings.failureMode: After canceling edit mode while on a reader-mode page, the address bar displays the internal 'http://localhost/reader-mode/page?url=...' URL instead of clearing it.
findings.title: cancelEditMode now propagates internal reader-mode URL into the address bar

findings.description: recordReaderModeTelemetry changed the switch to 'case .available: false' / 'default: true' (base: .available -> true, default -> false). The inline comment 'will be enabled after action gets executed' documents that .available means the tap will enable reader mode, so isEnabled should be true; the new code reports false when enabling and true when disabling. The wrong value is passed to toolbarTelemetry.readerModeButtonTapped on every reader mode button tap.
findings.failureMode: The toolbar.reader_mode_button_tapped Glean event records the inverted enabled state for every reader mode tap, corrupting analytics data.

findings.description: Line 78 uses global parseInt(e.target.value) while every sibling field (this file's Within input, and the other three new components) uses Number(...). biome.json sets style.useNumberNamespace to "error", so `biome ci` in the ui-v2-checks Lint job fails on this line. Semantically it also differs: parseInt("") returns NaN (vs 0), parseInt("1e5") returns 1 (vs 100000), and parseInt("2.5") silently truncates to 2, storing a wrong threshold.
findings.failureMode: CI lint job (biome ci) fails; on edge inputs the threshold is stored as NaN or silently truncated.
findings.title: Bare parseInt violates Biome useNumberNamespace and changes threshold semantics

findings.description: The onChange handler does e.target.value.split("\n") without filtering blank lines. Since split always returns at least one element, lines.length > 0 is always true and the undefined fallback is dead code: clearing the field stores [""] and any blank line adds a "" entry to trigger.expect. Server-side, matches("", event) (src/prefect/server/events/schemas/events.py:250) is false for every event, so a Reactive custom trigger with expect=[""] can never fire (empty expect would match any event), while a Proactive one treats "" as a never-arriving expected event and fires every within window.
findings.failureMode: Users who clear the field or leave blank lines silently create a reactive automation that can never trigger, or a proactive one that fires spuriously each window.
findings.title: Cleared Expected Events textarea stores expect=[""], breaking the custom trigger

findings.description: In setupToolbarConstraints, the diff changed `toolbar.leadingAnchor.constraint(equalTo: leftSkeletonAddressBar.trailingAnchor)` to `rightSkeletonAddressBar.trailingAnchor`. Per setupSkeletonAddressBarsLayout, rightSkeletonAddressBar.leadingAnchor is pinned to the container's trailingAnchor and its width equals container width minus UX.skeletonBarWidthOffset, so rightSkeletonAddressBar.trailingAnchor sits roughly one full container-width to the RIGHT of the container's trailing edge. The toolbar's leading is now required to be greater than its trailing (still pinned to rightSkeletonAddressBar.leadingAnchor), i.e. a negative width. Whenever toolbarHelper.isSwipingTabsEnabled is true (Nimbus toolbarRefactorFeature.swipingTabs on iPhone, per ToolbarHelper), Auto Layout cannot satisfy these required constraints and breaks one, leaving the address toolbar misplaced or collapsed.
findings.failureMode: Unsatisfiable Auto Layout constraints at runtime: 'Unable to simultaneously satisfy constraints' logging and the address toolbar laid out with a broken horizontal position whenever the swiping-tabs feature is enabled.
findings.title: Toolbar leading anchor pinned to wrong skeleton view

findings.description: The rename of pageActionStack to trailingPageActionStack was applied incorrectly in updateToolbarLayout: the stacks array now contains browserActionStack.arrangedSubviews twice and omits trailingPageActionStack.arrangedSubviews. updateActionStack sets `button.alpha = 0` for any button not already in the stack's arrangedSubviews, and updateToolbarLayout is the only place those alphas are animated/set back to 1.0 — in both the animated and non-animated branches. Trailing page action buttons (e.g. reader mode/reload icons supplied via config.trailingPageActions) that are newly added therefore remain at alpha 0 permanently.
findings.failureMode: Newly added trailing page-action buttons stay invisible (alpha 0) after every toolbar configuration update, so page action icons on the right side of the location bar never appear.
findings.title: Trailing page action buttons never get alpha restored

findings.description: The rename was also applied incorrectly in updateActionSpacing: `hasPageActions` now checks `!leadingPageActionStack.arrangedSubviews.isEmpty` where the base checked the (trailing) pageActionStack. locationDividerView is constrained between locationView.trailingAnchor and trailingPageActionStack.leadingAnchor, so its width must reflect trailing page actions. Now, when a config supplies trailing page actions but no leading page actions the divider collapses to width 0, and when leading actions exist without trailing actions the divider renders against empty space.
findings.failureMode: The separator between the URL field and the trailing page-action icons is shown or hidden based on the wrong stack, producing a missing or stray divider for asymmetric page-action configurations.
findings.title: Divider width keyed off wrong page-action stack

findings.description: The refactor of setupSkeletonAddressBarsLayout adds `let isLandscape = UIApplication.shared.statusBarOrientation.isLandscape` whose value is never used — no layout adjustment consumes it despite the comment claiming one. The line introduces an unused-immutable-value warning and a deprecation warning ('statusBarOrientation' was deprecated in iOS 13.0) into the Client target; it also uses UIApplication.shared directly rather than a protocol abstraction, contrary to the repository's dependency-abstraction rule (AGENTS.md rule 8). No enabled SwiftLint rule or warnings-as-errors flag turns this into a build failure, so impact is limited to warnings and dead code.
findings.failureMode: Two new compiler warnings (unused value, deprecated API) and dead code on every build; no functional effect because the computed value is discarded.
findings.title: Dead isLandscape read uses deprecated statusBarOrientation

findings.description: CodeExecutorJinja2TemplateRenderer.render_template is annotated '-> str' but returns `rendered`, which is `str | None` because `result.get("result")` may be None. Verified by running the project-pinned basedpyright 1.31.7 on the changed files: it reports 'Type "str | None" is not assignable to return type "str"' at template_renderer.py:40, so the required `make type-check` / CI `dev/basedpyright-check` gate (style.yml:52) fails. The None branch is also a real contract hole in the new injection seam: a custom code_executor whose transform_response omits "result" yields None, which propagates to `len(rendered)` in TemplateTransformNode._run and raises an uncaught TypeError. Fix: raise TemplateRenderError when rendered is None instead of returning it.
findings.failureMode: `uv run --directory api --dev basedpyright` fails on the changed file, blocking the type-check gate; a custom executor without a "result" key crashes _run with TypeError.
findings.title: render_template returns str | None despite -> str annotation (basedpyright reportReturnType error)

Trailing page actions carry the reload, stopLoading, readerMode and summarizer buttons per AddressBarState.trailingPageActions, so those icons never appear. findings.description: setupToolbarConstraints now anchors toolbar.leadingAnchor to rightSkeletonAddressBar.trailingAnchor (base anchored it to leftSkeletonAddressBar.trailingAnchor). setupSkeletonAddressBarsLayout pins rightSkeletonAddressBar.leadingAnchor to the container's trailingAnchor and its width to container width minus 32, so the right bar's trailing edge sits at roughly 2*W-32 while toolbar.trailingAnchor is still pinned to the right bar's leading edge at W. For any container wider than 32pt this requires toolbar.leading > toolbar.trailing, an impossible constraint set that Auto Layout must break whenever toolbarHelper.isSwipingTabsEnabled is true (iPhone swiping-tabs feature). findings.title: Toolbar pinned to the wrong skeleton bar produces unsatisfiable constraints

findings.description: updateActionSpacing now computes hasPageActions from leadingPageActionStack.arrangedSubviews; the base checked pageActionStack, i.e. the renamed trailingPageActionStack. The locationDividerView is constrained between locationView and trailingPageActionStack (line 272) and is visible (backgroundColor = colors.layer1), so its width should depend on trailing actions. When trailing actions exist but leading is empty (e.g. homepage states where isHomepage empties leadingPageActions while trailing still holds reload/stopLoading), the divider collapses to 0; when only leading actions exist while trailing is empty (isEmptySearch), a stray divider and dead gap render next to an empty stack. Fix: check trailingPageActionStack.arrangedSubviews.
findings.failureMode: The separator between the URL field and the trailing page actions is hidden in states where it should be shown and shown (plus extra dead space) in states where the trailing stack is empty.
findings.title: Divider width keyed off wrong action stack

findings.description: setupSkeletonAddressBarsLayout adds 'let isLandscape = UIApplication.shared.statusBarOrientation.isLandscape' which is never used, so it generates an unused-immutable-value warning and a deprecation warning (statusBarOrientation was deprecated in iOS 13; the Client target builds with SWIFT_TREAT_WARNINGS_AS_ERRORS = NO so these surface as warnings). The comment promises landscape layout adjustments but no constraint uses the value; the codebase's orientation checks use UIWindow.isLandscape or UIDevice.current.orientation. findings.failureMode: Adds dead code plus two new compiler warnings (unused variable, deprecated API) on every build; the advertised landscape adjustment never happens.
findings.title: Dead isLandscape variable uses deprecated statusBarOrientation

findings.description: write_and_make_executable now returns Result<(), FileWriteError> but is used with ? inside prepare_tools, which returns crate::Result<PathBuf> (crate::Error). error.rs only provides #[from] impls for concrete types (io::Error, anyhow::Error, etc.); there is no From<FileWriteError> and no blanket From<E: Error>, and ? performs a single From::from so it cannot chain through anyhow::Error. The five ? call sites at lines 232, 239, 245, 251 and 259 therefore fail to compile.
findings.failureMode: tauri-bundler fails to compile on Linux (the module is cfg(target_os = "linux")-gated), breaking the crate build and the clippy CI job on ubuntu-latest.
findings.title: FileWriteError has no From impl for crate::Error — E0277 on every ? call site

findings.description: The base version wrote the file first and then set permissions; the new code calls fs::set_permissions(path, ...) before fs::write. findings.title: set_permissions runs before write, failing on non-existent tool files

findings.failureMode: Every fresh AppImage bundling run fails with 'Failed to set permissions: No such file or directory'.

findings.failureMode: Every `tauri ios`/`tauri android` dev/build run errors out with 'app configuration is missing an identifier' even when the config defines a valid identifier.
findings.title: original_identifier reads the `bundle` object instead of top-level `identifier`

findings.description: The rewritten extractSlotFromKeysResult() iterates with 'j <= keys_result->numkeys' (base used 'j <'), so it performs one extra iteration. On that iteration it reads keys_result->keys[numkeys] out of bounds: for numkeys<6 it reads a zeroed/stale keysbuf entry (pos=0 -> argv[0], the command name); for numkeys==6 it reads past keysbuf into the 'keys' pointer field; for numkeys>6 it reads past the heap-allocated keys array. It then writes slot_buffer[numkeys], a 4-byte heap buffer overflow past the malloc'd region. Because the extra slot almost never equals first_slot, the function returns CLUSTER_CROSSSLOT for virtually every keyed command; preprocessCommand (server.c:4143) then sets CLIENT_READ_CROSS_SLOT, and getSlotFromCommand callers (cluster_asm.c:754,3456) likewise misbehave.
findings.failureMode: In cluster mode every keyed command is rejected with a cross-slot error (or, with >=6 keys or garbage pos, dereferences argv[garbage] and corrupts the heap via slot_buffer[numkeys]), so the server effectively cannot serve keyed traffic and may crash.
findings.title: Off-by-one loop bound reads/writes past keys_result and slot_buffer, breaking every keyed command in cluster mode

findings.description: Line 1110 calls malloc() and lines 1120/1124 call free() directly. AGENTS.md rule 2 requires all dynamic allocations in src/ to use zmalloc/zcalloc/zrealloc and all deallocations to use zfree so memory is tracked in used_memory. This allocation bypasses memory accounting and, because the malloc return is never checked, a failed allocation leads to a NULL dereference at slot_buffer[j] on line 1115 instead of zmalloc's controlled abort.
findings.failureMode: Memory used by slot extraction is invisible to Redis's used_memory accounting (undermining maxmemory enforcement), and on allocation failure the server segfaults on a NULL write rather than aborting cleanly.
findings.title: Direct malloc()/free() used instead of zmalloc/zfree, violating repo memory mandate; return value unchecked

findings.description: RolesGuard treats the @Roles value as a minimum role: hasMinimumRole returns checkRoleIndex <= requiredRoleIndex over TEAM_ROLES=[TEAM_OWNER, TEAM_ADMIN, TEAM_MEMBER], so a plain MEMBER membership satisfies @Roles("TEAM_MEMBER"). The sibling endpoint OrganizationsTeamsInviteController uses @Roles("TEAM_ADMIN") for the same operation, and the tRPC createInviteHandler gates on fallbackRoles [OWNER, ADMIN]; the PR description also states the endpoint requires TEAM_ADMIN. A non-admin member can therefore create invite tokens that let arbitrary users join the team, and the added e2e test expecting 403 for members will receive 200 and fail.
findings.failureMode: Regular team members can call POST /v2/teams/:teamId/invite and mint invite links (privilege escalation vs the admin-only contract), and the member-gets-403 e2e test fails.
findings.title: Wrong role: TEAM_MEMBER allows non-admin members to mint invite links

findings.description: The diff changes the new-token branch to return `token: newToken.identifier`, but identifier is the constant string `invite-link-for-teamId-${teamId}` (set in the same create call at line 90). The returned value is constant across calls for a team, is not the redeemable token, and is not contained in inviteLink (which embeds the hex token), so both the new e2e spec and the existing organizations-teams-invite e2e spec assertions `inviteLink.toContain(data.token)` and `data.token != firstToken` fail; any API consumer redeeming data.token hits `verificationToken.findFirst({token})` and gets nothing.

findings.title: createInvite returns verificationToken.identifier instead of the secret token

findings.description: Base code was `if (!isOrgContext) { return teamInviteLink; }` — regular teams got `${WEBAPP_URL}/teams?token=` and org-context teams got `${WEBAPP_URL}/signup?token=&callbackUrl=<getting-started>`. The diff flips it to `if (isOrgContext)`, so org/sub-team invites now return the plain /teams link while regular team invites route through signup with a getting-started callback — the opposite of the variable names (teamInviteLink/orgInviteLink) and of the PR's own documented behavior.

findings.title: Inverted isOrgContext check swaps invite link formats

findings.description: The deleted line `keyword_like_val = f"%{keyword[:30].encode('unicode_escape').decode('utf-8')}%".replace(r"\u", r"\\u")` converted non-ASCII keywords into their \uXXXX form so they match the stored text: WorkflowRun.inputs/outputs are LongText columns written via `json.dumps(...)` (ensure_ascii=True, e.g. sqlalchemy_workflow_execution_repository.py:152 and models/workflow.py:702), so non-ASCII content is stored literally as \uXXXX escapes. The replacement `escaped_keyword = escape_like_pattern(keyword_trimmed)` searches for the raw UTF-8 characters, which never match the \u-escaped JSON text. Reached via console endpoint `get_paginate_workflow_app_logs(..., keyword=args.keyword)` in controllers/console/app/workflow_app_log.py. Any non-ASCII keyword (e.g. Chinese) now silently returns no rows.
findings.failureMode: Searching workflow app logs with a non-ASCII keyword returns empty results even when matching runs exist, because the stored JSON text contains \uXXXX escapes the new pattern no longer produces.
findings.title: Workflow log keyword search regresses for non-ASCII input

findings.description: `escape_like_pattern(query)` escapes %, _ and \ with a backslash prefix (e.g. `test\_data`), but the SQL was changed to `WHERE text LIKE ? ESCAPE '|'`, which declares `|` — not `\` — as the escape character. The backslashes therefore become literal characters and the unescaped `_`/`%` still act as wildcards. In the LIKE fallback path of `search_by_full_text` (used when `IRIS_TEXT_INDEX` is unset), any query containing `%`, `_`, or `\` returns wrong results: e.g. searching '50%' requires the text to contain a literal backslash, so it returns nothing.
findings.failureMode: Full-text search on the IRIS backend returns empty/incorrect results for queries containing %, _ or \ when falling back to LIKE matching.
findings.title: IRIS LIKE fallback declares ESCAPE '|' but pattern is backslash-escaped

findings.description: `filter_clauses.append(f"... ESCAPE '\\\\'")` emits `ESCAPE '\\'` in the generated SQL. Every connection created by this class runs `SET cz.sql.string.literal.escape.mode = 'quote'` (_configure_connection, line 148), and in quote mode backslash is a literal character, so the literal `'\\'` is two characters. SQL requires the LIKE ESCAPE expression to be a single character, so `_search_by_like` — the fallback used when full-text MATCH_ALL search raises — produces a query the engine rejects, and the exception propagates out of `search_by_full_text`.
findings.failureMode: Every LIKE fallback search on the ClickZetta backend fails with a SQL error because the ESCAPE clause specifies an invalid two-character escape string.
findings.title: ClickZetta ESCAPE clause is a two-character literal under quote escape mode

findings.description: The new function uses `escapedPattern` as a local variable name. The repository compliance rules (AGENTS.md rule 16) require snake_case for all Python variables and list camelCase variable names as a failure criterion.
findings.failureMode: New code violates the repository's mandatory snake_case naming convention for variables.

findings.title: original_identifier always None after reading "bundle" key

Invalid tauri.conf.json/tauri.conf.json5 files are no longer reported and the CLI no longer exits non-zero on schema violations. Fix: restore `||`.

Callers xcode_script.rs:145 and android_studio_script.rs:98 invoke merge_with to apply cli_options.config; on iOS this is the only path applying those overrides to inner. findings.title: merge_with discards merged config; --config overrides silently ignored

findings.description: Line 153 (`let schema: JsonValue = serde_json::from_str(include_str!("../../config.schema.json")).expect("Failed to parse config schema bundled in the tauri-cli");`) is 156 characters. The repo rustfmt.toml sets max_width = 100 and AGENTS.md rule 3 requires `cargo fmt --all -- --check` to pass; rustfmt would split this method chain, so the fmt gate fails. findings.title: New line exceeds rustfmt max_width, breaking cargo fmt --check

AGENTS.md rule 13 requires UI measurements to be defined in a nested UX struct, and its failure criteria list 'UI constants and magic numbers scattered throughout the implementation code as literals'. Grep confirms no other file referenced DownloadToast.UX, so the removal compiles, but the changed lines now violate the mandated UX-struct convention.

findings.title: DownloadToast: UX struct removed, magic number 40 inlined as literals

findings.description: The replaced line was `keyword_like_val = f"%{keyword[:30].encode('unicode_escape').decode('utf-8')}%".replace(r"\u", r"\\u")`, which converted non-ASCII characters to the \uXXXX form and doubled the backslash so LIKE's default escape matched it literally. WorkflowRun.inputs and WorkflowRun.outputs are stored via json.dumps (api/models/workflow.py lines 702-703), which emits non-ASCII as \uXXXX, so a keyword like '你好' previously produced a pattern that matched the stored JSON text. escape_like_pattern only escapes \, %, _ and leaves '你好' as-is, so the new keyword_like_val never matches the \uXXXX-escaped column contents.

findings.description: escape_like_pattern escapes %, _ and \ by prefixing a backslash, but the new SQL clause is `WHERE text LIKE ? ESCAPE '|'`, which makes '|' the escape character instead of '\'. A query such as '50%' produces the bound pattern '%50\% discount%', which under ESCAPE '|' requires a literal backslash in the text; stored content '50% discount' therefore does not match. Likewise a '|' character in the user query is left unescaped and gains escape powers (e.g. 'a|b' matches 'ab' but not 'a|b').
findings.failureMode: On IRIS deployments with IRIS_TEXT_INDEX disabled, full-text search returns wrong or empty results whenever the query contains %, _, \ or |.
findings.title: IRIS LIKE fallback declares ESCAPE '|' but pattern is escaped with backslash
